_note: Frontier economy numbers (F2). F0.2 values approved by Tim 2026-11-02; everything else is a placeholder for Tim to tune. Time units: 'ticks' = economy ticks (1 per cadenceTicks sim ticks).

workers._note: placeholder, Tim to tune (L3.5/L3.6). Costs come from town stock and population when ordered. trainTicks, harvestTicks and clearTicks are sim ticks (20/second); training is sequential at the hall. load is stock per trip; harvested spots take longer to work as their pieces regrow. range is measured from the town hall. spawnRadius is proximity in world units; spawnPerTick bounds new entities globally; pathCacheSize bounds reusable navigation paths. hp and model are civilian stand-ins. logEntries caps saved delivery history per town.
workers._overworkNote: Tim 2026-11-06 22:23, placeholder: a spot card calls workers extra once more than this share of the spot's value is worked out (live estimate)

carts._note: Tim 2026-11-06 21:05-21:19, placeholders, Tim to tune: work camps store worker drop-offs up to cap; free ox carts per camp run a relay at speed (units/s, running speed) to the nearest hall or storehouse, each taking share of the camp stock (at most maxLoad); a full camp sends workers on to the hall or a storehouse. A cart beyond free is bought at the camp for extraCost, up to max. roadFactor = straight line x this for trip time; waitTicks = recheck an empty camp
carts._stopEdgeNote: Tim 2026-11-10: a drawn cart stops at the edge of the camp and of the hall or storehouse (this share of the building footprint from its centre), not at their centres; trip times unchanged.
carts._viewRadiusNote: Tim 2026-11-07: a moving cart is drawn while any of your units is within this (about 1.25 zoomed-out screens)
carts._workerPerMinNote: rough gather rate of one worker near a camp, only for the camp card line Carts keep up with about N workers

workers._campReachNote: Tim 2026-11-06 rich nodes, placeholder, Tim to tune: workers also reach spots within campReach of a built lumber camp or quarry (so far rich deposits need a work camp)
workers._laneNote: Tim 2026-11-10: each gathering worker walks its own lane, a fixed offset of min to max units beside the planned route with a small sway, so workers do not stack on the route, at the resource or at the drop-off; drawn position only, trip times unchanged. buildingPad = extra units worker routes keep from town building boxes. At a war camp workers drop at the edge of the camp building (its radius), on the side they come from.
workers._stuckNote: Tim 2026-11-05: after stuckGiveUp failed route retries a worker jumps to open ground within rescueReach; if still stuck it reappears at the nearest drop-off, hands in its cargo and goes idle
workers._dropoffsNote: Tim 2026-11-07: storehouses take no worker drop-offs (they only raise storage); a camp takes only its own resource (campTakes)

townGrid._buildingCollide: blocking box of placed buildings as a share of their tiles (Tim 2026-11-07: full tiles felt too big; 0.7 to 0.55 the same day, still invisible walls at the sides, now that placed art is capped by townArt._placedFootprint)
townGrid._note: placeholder, Tim to tune (L3.1): cellSize = world units per cell; radius = the town work range the grid covers; coreRadius = starting core where housing and work zones may go; corePerTier = core growth per town hall tier above 1; clearedRadius = cells round the hall that start cleared; hallRoadReserve = cells reserved around the hall for roads; cliffMargin = cells that roads and farm zones keep back from unbuildable ground

opening._note: placeholder, Tim to tune: preserve a townsperson for food/building and the first worker's training ryo when paying for projects

buildUI._note: placeholder, Tim to tune: presentation settings; zone buttons, overlays and valid drag previews share these colors

placeCosts._note: placeholder, Tim to tune (L3.2): per cell, paid at once when a road, wall or gate is placed; buildings use their own cost and queue as projects

zones._note: placeholder, Tim to tune (L3.3, numbers from the approved L3.0 table): per kind char = grid letter; coreOnly = core cells only; stages = looks per level (stage 0 = zoned, empty); needs: food = needs the town fed, workersPerCell = workers each grown cell wants, roadReach = a road (or the hall, hallIsRoad) within this many cells to grow; housing = people per cell per level; output = per cell per level per economy tick; inputs = paid per unit made; trait = traitEffects factor (fertile soil); growTicks = healthy economy ticks per stage; abandonTicks = short ticks before abandoned; governorCells = cells the governor zones at once. healthyAt = health needed to grow; shortBelow = health that counts as short; clearTicks = healthy ticks to clear an overgrown zoned cell. fromBuilding = old building types that migrate to zones (and what the governor's house/farm/workshop rules mean in grid towns).
zones._roadsConnectNote: Tim 2026-11-05: only roads and gates linked to the town hall (a chain of road/gate cells, diagonals join, reaching within roadReserve + 1 cells of the hall) give zones road access

tiers._costNote: Tim 2026-11-05: upgrade costs = 75% of the current tier (was 90%, Tim 2026-11-05 evening: leave stock to run the next tier)'s base storage cap (storage.caps) in timber, stone and goods
tiers._note: Economy balance B3, placeholder, Tim to tune: town hall tiers (tier 1 first, set at founding). ring = build radius in world units from the hall for every zone, town building, wall and gate (roads and work camps may go outside); cells = most zoned cells per zone kind; placed = most of each placed building type (camps counts lumber_camp + quarry together); workers = most workers incl. training; upgrade = what moving UP to this tier costs (pop counts townspeople + workers) and how many economy ticks it takes.

upkeep._note: Economy balance B5, placeholder, Tim to tune: paid every economy tick. The first freeLevels grown zone levels of a town are free; above that, zones pay their rate per grown level (scaled by the share above the free allowance). Short zone upkeep lowers that zone's health (less output and housing; long shortages abandon it, then it recovers). buildings = per built placed building; lines = per wall (w) / gate (g) cell; workerWage = per worker incl. training (short wages show as waiting). goodsByStage = goods per housing cell at stage 1, 2, 3: housing levels up to stage 2+ only while goods are paid; short goods never lower a level, they cost goodsShortMood of mood.

townsfolk._note: Tim 2026-11-07, placeholder, Tim to tune: citizens wandering your towns in peacetime, one per perPeople of the population, at most max[tier] (Camp, Village, Town); they go back to the town hall at night or while enemies are inside the town ring (hurry = speed factor then). Only while one of your units is within viewRadius of the hall. speed in units per second. Tim 2026-11-08: models default to the capital's walker mix (civilians.json types by count); roam = how far from the town hall they walk, by tier (world units). Tim 2026-11-10: max +1 per tier for the town dogs (civilians.json town_dog)

arrivals._note: Economy balance B7, placeholder, Tim to tune: a new townsperson walks out of the town hall to a house (Tim 2026-11-05) when the player's units are within workers.spawnRadius (else they just arrive). models = civilian looks picked in turn (workers use laborer); speed = units per second; fxTicks = how long the +1 and the level-up scaffold/dust show (sim ticks).

market._note: Economy pass 2 D (Tim 2026-11-05): a built market sells goods above the town's keep level (setMarketKeep; default keep) at price ryo per goods, at most perTick goods each economy tick

storage._note: Economy balance B2, placeholder, Tim to tune: most of each resource a town can hold. caps = by town hall tier (tier 1 first); each built storehouse adds perStorehouse; uncapped resources have no limit. Stock already above the cap stays but cannot grow; workers on a full resource wait (status Store full).

rates._foodNote: F0.2: food eaten per person per economy tick
rates._growthNote: F0.2: +1 person every 60 economy ticks while housing is free and food is in surplus
rates._buildersNote: placeholder, Tim to tune: most workers that can build one project at once
rates._foodShortNote: placeholder, Tim to tune: food is 'short' when stock covers fewer than this many economy ticks of eating; short food fills farm jobs first
rates._idleTaxNote: Tim 2026-11-05: idle townsfolk pay this share of tax; employed pay full
rates._taxNote: placeholder, Tim to tune: ryo per person per review (every mood.reviewTicks economy ticks), times mood/100
rates._shipmentNote: F0.2: units per second (used from F3)

values._note: F0.2: frontier goods sold in the capital: goods 4 ryo, timber 1, stone 1; food 1 is a placeholder. Used to price projects against a town budget

governor._upgradeGoalNote: 2026-11-06 soak fix, placeholder: while the next hall tier's goods cost is not in stock the governor aims for enough goods income to save it within this many game minutes (more work cells, within the tier cell cap)
governor._selfRunNote: Tim 2026-11-05: with initiative On the governor lays road spurs (up to roadSpur cells, only if they open roadSpurMinCells zonable cells) and trains a worker when all are busy, keeping trainRyoKeep ryo and trainGoodsKeep goods
governor._goodsProfitNote: Tim 2026-11-05: the governor adds work cells while running goods income (per minute, one-off spends left out) is below this
governor._foodPlentyNote: Tim 2026-11-05: food at or above this share of its storage cap never counts as falling (no farm suggestion)
governor._initiativeBudget: value (data.values) a governor with initiative may spend on his own suggestions per budgetWindowReviews when the town has no budget set

priorities._note: placeholder, Tim to tune: job fill order per settlement priority (after short food and builders)

alerts._note: placeholder, Tim to tune (F4.4c). B7: growth alerts (town grew past a milestone of popMilestone people, housing full) share one cooldown of growthCooldownEcon economy ticks per town so they never spam

need._note: Tim 2026-11-06: how badly a town needs you (all-towns window Need column, worst first). Score = sum of weights of what is wrong now; attack/destroyed count for recentEcon economy ticks after the alert. Placeholder, Tim to tune

alerts._upgradeNote: Tim 2026-11-05: while the town can afford its next hall tier, a reminder alert repeats every upgradeEveryEcon economy ticks

mood._note: placeholder, Tim to tune (F2.5b). mood 0-100 = weighted food, safety and taxes factors, reviewed every reviewTicks economy ticks

traitEffects._note: E4 placeholders, Tim to tune. soil: farm output factor by soil level; nodeKinds: which resource node kind a building type needs within the town's traits.nodes; noNodeFactor: output factor with no such node (1 = core resources work anywhere, Tim 2026-11-04: nodes are a bonus only; lower it to make nodes required); each extra node adds nodeBonus up to nodeMax. Water (housing per well) and defence (stockade bonus) wait for wells and the F6/F7 defence rules.

townArt._note: E5 placeholders, Tim to tune: which existing building cutout (data/art.json) draws each frontier building type until town art exists

_stationParts._note: Tim 2026-11-07: the 3x2 railway station is drawn as the ticket hall (hall) and the engine shed (shed), each fit to fit cells wide (like _placedFootprint).

townArt._noBlockNote: Tim 2026-11-11: art that blocks no walking. Every other town, zone and war camp building blocks the ground its art stands on (art/cutouts.json blocks, tools/build_art_blockers.py; wall height per art: art.json blockWall).

_placedFootprint._note: Tim 2026-11-07, placeholder, Tim to tune: largest width a placed building's art may take, in town cells (11 world units each); bigger art is shrunk to fit, smaller is left. Zone houses use zoneFootprint (0.8 cell).

_zones._note: placeholder, Tim to tune (L3.7): cutouts by zone growth stage; one farmhouse per houseEvery cells. zoned = art on a zoned cell at stage 0 (housing: building site 1; stage 1 is site 2, then house, large house); abandoned = ruin art for an abandoned kind (farms keep the grey tint).

_ground._note: placeholder, Tim to tune (L3.7): art-only dirt foundation, road and crop decals; sizes are fractions of a town cell except foundationRadius (world units).

_walls._note: placeholder, Tim to tune (L3.7): existing fence segments and an open gate stand-in; no collision changes.

_spots._note: placeholder, Tim to tune (L3.7): art scale by full/harvested/sapling stage, nearby display and minimap threshold; does not change harvesting or collision.

glow._note: Tim 2026-11-05: ground glow under discovered resource spots and nodes (render only). opacity/pulse = brightness and its swing, periodMs = pulse time, reach = show radius x the prop radius, pad/minRadius = glow beyond the pieces, nodeRadius = big node glow, bigScale = rich spots and nodes

rich._note: Tim 2026-11-06: rich deposits get a bigger soft warm wash (scale x their radius, warmth = mix toward lamplight, no pulse) and a flat badge with the kind character (石 stone, 鉱 ore, 木 forest, 魚 fish, 稲 fertile) that fades in between iconFrom and iconFull zoom-out (viewScale); iconSize = share of screen height. Placeholders, Tim to tune

forage._note: placeholder, Tim to tune: a founded town with no lumber camp gathers timberPerIdle per idle person per economy tick by hand, up to cap in stock, so it can never be stuck at 0 timber

townLights._note: E5 placeholder, Tim to tune: stone lanterns (data/art.json) set beside each finished building of this type, how many (max 2). They glow at night. Houses, the town hall and the stockade already have lit windows in their art.

automatic._note: placeholder, Tim to tune: decorative lights at regular developed grid corners; no cost, collision or build-cell use

goals._note: Goal card after founding (Tim 2026-11-06, placeholders to tune): Lay out your town (road, housing and farm cells), Put workers to work (workers on a resource spot), Grow to Village (tier 2), Open a Market; holdBusinesses = capital businesses the hold-the-capital row asks for.

war._note: F6 war, checkpoint 1 (Tim 2026-11-10), placeholders, Tim to tune. circleRadius = war circle round the target's town hall. Planting the war camp banner is the declaration: band = banner distance from the hall, the town's build ring + inner to + outer (widenStep = how far the outer edge widens at a time when no ground in the band can be built on, up to the circle); placeRange = most distance from the hero to the banner spot; campSpacing = least distance to another war camp banner; cooldownDays = game days after a war ends before anyone can declare on that town again; historyMax = ended wars kept in the save.

pack._note: Pack for war (checkpoint 2): what the hero may carry to a war camp. max per resource, min = least amount if any is carried (0 = none needed). The pack is optional: a banner can be planted without one. Ryo has no limit. In the city only ryo can be packed; timber and stone come from the clan's towns (packs from several towns add up).

camp._note: War camp (Tim 2026-11-10). startWorkers = workers the camp begins with; more are hired at the camp for workerCost ryo each from the war chest, up to workerCap in all (training time as town workers). Camp workers gather only the resources listed (no food) anywhere in the war circle outside the town build ring, and drop at the camp hall into the camp stock, which no town ever sees. gatherSpeed = camp-only gather factor (1 = normal).

war._buildNote: Checkpoint 4, placeholders, Tim to tune. chainDistance = most distance from a new camp building to another camp building (centres). builders = most camp workers building one site at once. buildings: cost = timber and stone paid from the camp stock when placed; buildTicks = sim ticks of work for one worker (3 workers build 3 times as fast); radius = ground the building takes (spacing); max = most per camp; needs = built types first (upgrade = the camp hall upgrade); cap = troop cap each built one adds. hallUpgrade = the camp hall upgrade (ryo from the war chest), built by workers like a site. Palisade, gate and the second-special building come in later checkpoints.

standIn._note: Checkpoint 4 stand-in defender until the bot general (8d), placeholders: a bot clan's town at war trains one grunt every trainTicks for ryo from its coffers, up to max, hallDistance from the hall; they go for attacker units within the town ring + reach.

dev._note: Dev build only: devStartWar gives the camp this pack when the attacker carries none.

units._note: War checkpoint 5 shared roster (Tim 2026-11-11 OK, enforcers at the barracks), placeholders, Tim to tune: ryo from the war chest per troop, trainTicks = sim ticks each (one at a time per building), at = camp buildings that train it, type = units.json type (one name, or one per clan faction), model = the body drawn per clan (stand-ins until the army kit art pass). War-only types (war_enforcer, army_archer, army_rifleman, sword_rider, mounted_pikeman) have no price in units.json, so they never show in a city hire menu. Clan specials come at checkpoint 7.

clanBonus._note: War checkpoint 5 placeholders, Tim to tune: per clan faction and roster unit, multipliers on ryo, trainTicks, hp and damage (missing = 1). Stat multipliers are set on each troop when it spawns.

cavalry._note: War checkpoint 5 placeholders, Tim to tune: a war.units entry with cavalry: true spawns already on a horse (horse = model per clan faction, hp = the rider's) and never gets off: no dismount on attack, hit or low health. It fights from the saddle at speed x its run speed. Rider and horse fall together.

founding._note: E1/E3 placeholders, Tim to tune. cost = ryo paid by the clan at founding; minSettlers must stand within gatherRadius of the hero; minSpacing = least distance to any other town or the capital (1600 from economy balance B4, Tim 2026-11-05: fewer, bigger towns; 600 rings never overlap); capitalSpacing = least distance to the capital point (Tim 2026-11-06: about 500 from the island gate, so a town can go up a short walk out); bots found only within botSiteRadius of a W1 site; startStock = what the settlers bring (no grind at the start); townHall is built at founding, firstProject is queued (unauthorized).
founding._placementNote: placeholder, Tim to tune: hall placement reach from hero and unit escape clearance in world units
founding._startWorkersNote: Tim 2026-11-05: free workers with every new town (on top of the settlers), in case there are no goods to train one

permit._note: E1 2026-11-05 placeholders, Tim to tune. A founding permit is bought at the Land Office (telegraph_office) and used up by the next founding. Player needs renown, crew and businesses held; bots need none of these (bots: false). ryo = permit price. maxTowns = towns a clan may found for now (C4 Influence raises it for the 2nd and 3rd town).
permit._townTierNote: Tim 2026-11-06: the Nth permit also needs one of your towns at this tier (2nd: Village, 3rd: Town); players only, like the other requirements

shinobi._note: Tim 2026-11-06: Shinobi hold no businesses, so they pay ryo instead

founding._graceNote: E1 2026-11-05: camp bandits leave a new town's people alone for this many days (inside graceRadius of the hall)

siteMenu._note: Choose-site menu at the island gate (E1): campWarn = warn when a bandit camp is this close to a site

bots._note: E6 2026-11-05 placeholders, Tim to tune. Bots go once the player founds a first town, or by fallbackDay anyway. Departures are staggerDays apart per bot. Site score = traits (soil+water+defense) + clan taste - travel cost/travelScale + a seeded random roll up to randomRoll; a bot picks at random among the topPick best free sites. reserve = ryo kept back on top of permit, settlers and founding cost.
bots._leaveNote: Tim 2026-11-11: the first bot leaves afterPlayerDays after the player's first town (the next staggerDays later), or from fallbackDay if the player has no town by then. A Yakuza or Kuroda bot first holds minBusinesses, for at most businessWaitDays past its day. Bots save for the trip only from their day on.
bots._richNodeNote: Tim 2026-11-06: site score bonus per rich deposit within workers.range + campReach of the site

traits._note: Computed from the terrain round the spot (sim/frontier/founding.js siteTraits). soilWeight/defenseWeight = what each terrain code adds per sample (average over the circle), then soilShare/defenseShare = [level 2 from, level 3 from]; water = distance to the nearest river, lake or sea: waterNear = [level 3 up to, level 2 up to]; nodes counts resource nodes within nodeRadius.

_buildingCostNote: Tim 2026-11-05: placed building costs (storehouse, camps, stockade, market) doubled in economy pass 2

town_hall._note: E3 placeholder, Tim to tune: tier 1 town hall, built at founding (F6.1 grows it); houses the first settlers

house._note: F0.2: housing 6, cost 15 timber; buildTicks placeholder, Tim to tune

farm._note: F0.2: 0.03 food per worker per tick; cost and jobs placeholder, Tim to tune

lumber_camp._note: F0.2: 0.02 timber per worker per tick; cost and jobs placeholder, Tim to tune

food_camp._note: Tim 2026-11-07, placeholder, Tim to tune: fish and forage work camp (fishing grounds and fertile ground give food); same cart and storage rules as the lumber camp; art forage_camp from frontier sheet 3 (frbuilds3)

quarry._note: F0.2: 0.015 stone per worker per tick; cost and jobs placeholder, Tim to tune

workshop._note: F0.2: 1 timber + 0.5 stone into 1 goods every 40 sim ticks (2 economy ticks) with 2 workers; cost placeholder, Tim to tune

storehouse._note: placeholder, Tim to tune; no storage cap yet

stockade._note: Tim 2026-11-06: 4-cell fort (size 2). garrison: your hero, crew and workers can shelter inside (capacity units), safe from attack and healing healFactor times faster; range = how close a unit must be to go in. hp (Tim 2026-11-06) = stockade health: hits on anyone inside go to the stockade; at 0 it is ruined and everyone piles out (enemies attacking the building itself waits for F7). Cost and times are placeholders, Tim to tune

capital._note: Tim 2026-11-07, placeholders to tune: the capital stable (the old rickshaw station art in the city) sells for clan ryo, no waiting, to a clan holding or having used a founding permit. What you buy waits on the island side of the gate. room: how many of each it adds to your stables' room.

room._note: Tim 2026-11-07: how many of each your stables can hold, by the town's tier (1, 2 Village, 3 Town); your limit is the sum over all your towns with a built stable. Owned ones are never taken away.

stable._note: Tim 2026-11-06/07, placeholders to tune: a placed building (no ryo costs). Horses, rickshaws and omnibuses are all made here by hand, one at a time on its production bar (seconds each, cost paid from town stock when queued, refunded on cancel); up to queue jobs wait on the bar and +5 queues five at once, up to the room its town's tier gives (stable.room); nothing is made on its own except one horse and one rickshaw for a bot clan. Click the stable or Space beside it opens the stable menu.

station._note: Tim 2026-11-06/07: omnibus station (coach house art), also the railway station (data/railways.json). Vehicles are made at the stable since 2026-11-07. reach: how close Space works; fightSeconds/enemyRange: no travel with a fight on.

infirmary._note: Tim 2026-11-06, placeholders to tune: your units within radius heal healFactor times faster; anyone knocked out on the island comes round at the nearest town's infirmary at full health (else at its hall at low health). One per Camp and Village, two per Town

market._note: Economy pass 2 D (Tim 2026-11-05): Village tier, 1 per town; sells goods above the town keep level for ryo (see market)
